notes: Header describes saved prior failure seeds, replay before novel generated cases, and advice to commit them so other test runs benefit. This is the corpus format's own operational description, not verification that a particular current harness consumes this file.

Two cc seed records preserve shrunk values consisting of one empty string and an empty collection, respectively. Exact64-hex identifiers in the appendix must remain unchanged for reproducibility; the comments give no assertion or root cause.

Two distinct cc seed IDs each annotate values as a single inner collection of65 zeros. Identical displayed shrunk inputs can arise from different generator seeds; they are not duplicate IDs. Width/cardinality observations come from the literal comments, not inferred data types or executed failures.

Final two cc seeds annotate Unicode/control-rich strings. The first has one string; the second two, beginning with escaped U+007F. Comments retain literal supplementary/BMP glyphs, escaped U+0080/U+000B and null escapes, spaces and ASCII text. Do not normalize or reinterpret these comments as a decoded byte encoding; they document shrunk shapes, while replay identity is the seed. The exact text is preserved below.
